forecasts.question: Will an Iranian official (Pezeshkian, Araghchi, or named Foreign Ministry spokesperson) make a public statement explicitly addressing the 14-point MOU on the record before EOD 2026-05-13?

No named Iranian official (Pezeshkian, Araghchi, Baghaei, Larijani, or Mojtaba Khamenei) made a public statement explicitly addressing the US-authored 14-point MOU by name before EOD May 13. Araghchi's May 12 PressTV statement addressed US negotiating conduct broadly; his BRICS travel on May 13 produced no on-record named-framework statement. Iranian state media framing through May 13 referenced Iran's own counter-proposal and general US negotiations — not the 14-point framework by title. Ambiguity rule invoked: no named-framework statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named Iranian official (Pezeshkian, Araghchi, Baghaei, Larijani, or Mojtaba Khamenei) is quoted directly by name in Reuters/AP/AFP/IRNA/Press TV/Tasnim addressing the specific 14-point framework or its terms (not generic 'reviewing US proposals'). Iran responded with Pezeshkian's 'never bow' (May 11) and Araghchi's 'US approach is the main obstacle' (May 12). Pakistan channel is dormant; Witkoff/Kushner Islamabad trip was cancelled in late April and has not been rescheduled — this indicator is CONTRADICTED, not merely unobserved. Araghchi's travel to BRICS India (May 13-14) signals diplomatic bandwidth directed elsewhere. Trump's presence in Beijing for Xi summit (May 14-15) creates a possible China-mediation bridging pathway, but no operational signing mechanism exists within five days — a signed memo would require reconvened talks, bridging the MOU-vs-counter-proposal gap, and principal confirmation from both sides.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm signing of a written memorandum; OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal/'agreement in principle' does not count. Trump-unilateral announcement without Iranian FM confirmation within 24 hours = NO.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At least two named official sources from each side, OR official document release by State Dept / Iranian Foreign Ministry / Pakistani Foreign Office acting as confirmed mediator. Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios reporting acceptable when both sides quoted.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If a memo is signed but Iran publicly disputes key terms within 72 hours: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (per JCPOA-2022 failure pattern). If signed by envoys but not publicly confirmed by principals (Trump/Pezeshkian) by horizon: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump-unilateral announcement without Iranian FM confirmation within 24 hours = NO.

forecasts.question: Will Iran formally and publicly reject the current MOU framework before EOD 2026-05-18?
forecasts.delta_reason: Iran's posture through May 13 remains consistent with 'never bow / conditions not met' rhetoric rather than formal explicit rejection. Pezeshkian's 'never bow' (May 11) and Araghchi's 'US approach is obstacle' (May 12) do not constitute formal public rejection language per resolution criteria: neither statement uses the required rejection vocabulary (rad, mardud, rejected, refused) applied specifically to the US-authored or jointly-labelled 14-point framework. Iran submitted its own counter-proposal — which per ambiguity rule explicitly resolves NO for formal rejection. Baghaei's characterisation of Iran's own 14-point plan as 'exclusively focused on ending war' positions Iran as diplomatically engaged rather than walking away. Slight downward move reflects Iran's documented preference for tactical silence and counter-proposal posture over formal walk-away. NOTE: Counter-proposal language distinguishing Iran's own framework from the US-authored one is now embedded in resolution_criteria per DA hygiene flag.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran's Foreign Ministry, Pezeshkian, or Khamenei's office issues a public statement using rejection language (rad, mardud, rejected, refused) about the US-authored 14-point framework specifically. NO if Iran continues 'reviewing,' issues a counter-proposal, or uses its own separate 14-point plan language without explicitly rejecting the US document. Counter-proposal with modifications = NOT rejection (resolve NO). Iran's own 14-point plan references do not constitute rejection of the US framework.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Direct attributed quote in IRNA, Press TV, Tasnim, or Reuters/AP/AFP. Statement must name the US-authored framework, not generic 'US proposals' and not Iran's own counter-proposal.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Counter-proposal with modifications = NOT rejection (resolve NO). Walk-away from talks without explicit rejection statement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iran's own '14-point plan' references without explicit rejection of US framework = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Daily Hormuz transits stand at approximately 6-12 vessels per day as of May 12-13 — roughly 10-24% of the 50-vessel threshold. Lloyd's war-risk premiums remain at approximately 2.5% of hull value, well above the 1.5% indicator threshold. Maersk, MSC, and Frontline have not announced return to scheduled transit. The Trump-Xi summit (May 14-15) is the single most consequential near-term development, but even a strong Chinese commitment to press Iran does not immediately move vessel counts — any compliance pathway requires Iranian policy change, IRGC operational adjustment, Lloyd's re-rating, and major shipping line announcements, each with their own lead time. June 10 is 27 days away, providing some runway, but the current transit rate is so far below threshold that a YES outcome requires a near-linear chain of independent positive events. F6 also carries a baseline mismatch: the question text references '50%+ of pre-war ~120/day' as a parenthetical, but 50% of 120 = 60, not 50; Judge retains the 50/day absolute threshold specified in resolution_criteria and removes the parenthetical from delta context. Newsmax reporting of companies paying 'extortion tolls' for transit confirms Hormuz is partially traversable for dark-fleet vessels, but these do not count toward the Western-shipping threshold per ambiguity rule.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports at least 50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window. Dark-fleet or Iranian-flagged-only transits where Western insurers still refuse = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO per ambiguity rule.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned).
